seeds.title: Cross-record historical semantics vocabulary
seeds.summary: Define and apply one shared glossary for historical state semantics across attempts, promotions, concerns, graph patches, recovery records, and lane/worktree objects.
evidence: Attempts already distinguish stale_historical, but other record families have uneven semantics.
Promotion, concern, graph patch, and recovery objects need explicit distinctions among current, historical, superseded, revoked, reopened, archived, and removed states.
UI behavior should expose semantic reasons directly instead of inferring status from dimming, disappearance, or storage/archive behavior.
proposed_actions: Create a canonical semantic glossary and apply it consistently to all listed record families.
Add successor/predecessor links where supersession can occur.
Separate visibility policy (archived/hidden) from validity semantics (historical/revoked/superseded).

seeds.title: Project run chronology versus explicit relationships
seeds.summary: Same-project runs must not imply lineage; run-to-run relationships should be explicit metadata, while historical run state remains a focus/time classification.
evidence: Multiple runs in one project may be unrelated and should not imply predecessor/successor or supersession semantics.
Chronological order, shared repo, or naming similarity are insufficient to infer lineage.
Search and routing must preserve exact run identity and avoid cross-run collapse.
proposed_actions: Keep history views chronological-first by default.
Introduce explicit relationship labels only when metadata exists (e.g., derived from, retry of, continuation of).
Avoid UI copy that claims supersession by newer run unless explicit relationship metadata supports it.

seeds.title: Concern record model hardening
seeds.summary: Concern handling needs a stronger canonical record contract with explicit lifecycle semantics and relationships to source events, projections, and adjacent systems.
evidence: Current docs capture concern lifecycle states and canonical creators but remain sparse on exact record shape.
Concerns lag behind attempts/blocked/remediation in schema precision, merge/split/supersession rules, and linkage to corroboration/review/patch/recovery.
A useful split emerges: concern record (durable identity), concern source event/ref (supporting evidence), concern projection (surface-specific rendering).
proposed_actions: Define an explicit concern schema with stable identity, lifecycle, and lineage semantics.
Codify merge/split/supersession and reopened behavior for concern records.
Specify relationship contracts from concern records to reviews, corroboration outcomes, graph patches, and recovery outcomes.
